ModuleName: Analyzing User Testing Results and Iterative Redesign
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured topic outline covering the full workflow of usability testing analysis—from distinguishing quantitative and qualitative data, collecting and organizing findings via affinity diagrams and issue logs, classifying and root-causing errors, and prioritizing fixes using severity and impact frameworks—which instructors use to sequence lessons and learners use to navigate the module's core concepts.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A topic outline for the 'Analyzing User Testing Results and Iterative Redesign' module covering usability test data types, quantitative vs. qualitative findings, and iterative redesign concepts, which learners and instructors can use as a navigational overview of the module's subject matter.

Artifacts.Name: Foundations of Usability Test Data
Artifacts.Description: Covers the types of data generated by usability testing — including quantitative and qualitative categories, how each is measured, and what each can and cannot reveal — giving learners a foundation for interpreting test results accurately.

Artifacts.Name: Collecting and Organizing Test Data
Artifacts.Description: Explains how to transform raw observations, recordings, and notes from usability sessions into structured, actionable insights, guiding learners and instructors through systematic data collection and organization methods.

Artifacts.Name: Interpreting Error Analysis
Artifacts.Description: Teaches learners how to move beyond surface-level error observations to diagnose what user mistakes reveal about underlying interface problems, covering classification, interpretation, and the analytical process of error analysis.

Artifacts.Name: Prioritizing Usability Improvements
Artifacts.Description: Addresses how to evaluate and rank usability problems when resources are limited, helping learners apply frameworks for weighing severity, frequency, and impact to decide which issues to fix first in a realistic project context.

Artifacts.Name: Principles of Iterative Redesign
Artifacts.Description: Introduces the iterative redesign process — covering its core principles of hypothesis, change, testing, and evaluation in repeated cycles — and explains why multiple design passes based on real user feedback outperform single-pass design attempts.

Artifacts.Name: Implementing Redesign Changes in Prototypes
Artifacts.Description: Guides learners through translating usability test findings into deliberate, concrete prototype changes, covering how to implement redesign decisions in a way that produces a measurably improved next version of the design.

Artifacts.Name: Documenting and Communicating Redesign Outcomes
Artifacts.Description: Explains how to document the outcomes of a usability-driven redesign and communicate changes and rationale to stakeholders, emphasizing the role of clear reporting in building organizational memory and demonstrating evidence-based design value.
